messages.content: my sister is at home and i am at the library. she asks me to bring her book home. if i tell my friend what i am doing, can i say i will take the book home?
yes. both can work from the places you gave. your sister is talking about the book coming to where she is. you are talking about moving it from the library to home.
so bring and take are not always about two different things happening?
right. they can tell about the same book going from one place to another. the people and where they are help make the meaning clear.
say that simply.
both sentences can be about the same book going from the library to home. who is talking and where they are helps explain the word choice.
now write my sister question and my answer.
could you bring my book home? yes, i will take it home when i leave the library.
does that mean i already left?
no. the answer is a plan for when you leave. you have not said the journey has happened yet.
now i am home with the book. make my answer something that has happened.
i brought your book home. it is here with me.
what changed other than the word bring?
the time changed from a plan to something finished. the book has now moved, and you are at home rather than still at the library.
i hear music through a closed door. i know my brother likes that song. can i say he must be inside?
not from the music alone. someone else could be playing it, or the music could be on without him in the room. knowing he likes the song does not tell you where he is now.
what can i say that is true from what i heard?
you can say you heard that song through the door. you can also say your brother likes it if that is something you already know, but keep those as two details rather than saying he must be there.
make that simple.
you heard the song, and you know your brother likes it. you still do not know if he is in the room.
now i open the door and see my sister playing music on her phone. my brother is not there.
then the new information says your sister is there with the music. the first sound was not enough to choose your brother as the person inside.
give the last facts only.
your sister is in the room playing music on her phone. your brother is not there.
can i ask my brother later whether he was there before?
yes. not being there when you opened the door does not say where he was all day. you could ask whether he had been in the room before you came.
write that question.
were you in that room before i came in and saw my sister?
i have four containers. two are red and two are white. both red containers are empty, and only one white container is empty. how many empty containers are there?
there are three empty containers: the two red containers and one white container. the other white container is not empty in your example.
ask my question with containers.
i have two red containers and two white containers. both red containers and only one white container are empty. how many containers are empty?
now answer with only the number word.
three.
i put fruit in one red container. how many empty containers now?
there are two empty containers now: the other red container and one white container.
does putting fruit in the red container make a new container?
no. there are still four containers. one changed from empty to having fruit inside, but no new container was added.
answer simply.
no. there are still four containers, but only two are empty now.
now ask me which white container is empty without choosing one.
which of the white containers is empty?
write a story about a brother and sister writing one letter to their grandmother. they both want something different in it, and neither wants the other part taken out.

a brother and sister sat at the table with one piece of paper. he wanted to tell their grandmother about a book he had finished. she wanted to tell her about a flower growing near their door. at first, they both tried to start the letter. then the sister asked whether they had to choose only one thing. they wrote a short part about the book and another about the flower. at the end, each added a question for their grandmother. the letter was longer than their first idea, but there was still enough space on the paper.
make the last line simple.
the letter was longer than their first idea, but there was still enough space on the paper.
does one letter mean only one person can have a voice in it?
no. the story has one letter with something from both people. they can keep their different ideas while making one message together.
write their two questions, but do not choose the grandmother answers.
what are you reading now? are you growing any flowers?
keep it with now in a simple answer.
what are you reading now? is the flower near your window still growing?
what if they do not know whether their grandmother is growing flowers?
then are you growing any flowers is still a question they can ask. it does not say they know she has a specific flower near a window.
give the two questions without saying she must have a flower.
what are you reading now? are you growing any flowers?
i drew for a little while today. i do not think the picture is very good, but i liked doing it.
you can enjoy making a picture without having to choose it as your best work. what did you like about the time?
i liked looking at a simple cup and trying to put the shape on paper. i stopped thinking about other work for a few minutes.
then you had one small thing to look at. you can still want the picture to be better and enjoy the time you spent making it.
keep it simple.
you looked at one cup and tried drawing it. even if you want the picture to be better, you can still like the time you spent making it.
i want to tell a friend, but i do not want them to feel they have to say it is my best work.
you could say: i tried drawing a cup today. i am still learning, but i enjoyed the quiet time with it. that is about what you did, rather than asking your friend to say how good the picture is.
give only a simple message.
i drew a cup today. i am still learning, but i enjoyed the time i spent making it.
what if they ask to see it and i want to keep it to myself for now?
you can say: i would like to keep this one to myself for now, but i wanted to tell you i enjoyed trying. saying you drew does not mean you must show the drawing right away.
answer simply.
i would like to keep the drawing to myself for now. i just wanted to tell you i enjoyed trying it.
i started washing cups, and my father began reading later. for a while we did those things at the same time. can i say i washed cups while he read?
yes. while can put the washing and reading together for some of the time. they do not have to start or finish at the same moment.
say it simply.
yes. part of your washing happened at the same time as his reading. one could start before the other.
now make a little story from the facts i gave. do not say who finished first because i have not told you.
i started washing cups. later, my father began reading. for a while, i washed while he read. we were doing different things during part of the same time.
keep it simple.
i started washing cups. my father began reading later. for a while, i washed cups while he read.
if i add i finished before he did, what is clear now?
then you finished washing first, and his reading went on after that. the order of finishing is now clear, though it was not given before.
answer simply.
you finished washing first. your father was still reading after you finished.
now put the whole thing in two sentences.
i started washing cups before my father began reading, and for a while i washed while he read. i finished washing first, while he was still reading.
my sentence says my sister saw my aunt when she came home. i mean my sister came home, but i am not sure the sentence makes that clear.
you can make the person specific: when my sister came home, she saw my aunt. that puts your sister as the person coming home.
now make my aunt the one coming home instead.
my sister saw my aunt when my aunt came home.
can you make it shorter while keeping who came home clear?
when my aunt came home, my sister saw her.
ask my last request simply.
make it shorter, but keep who came home clear.
if i then say she brought a book, do you know for sure which person i mean?
not for sure from that alone. both people are still in the conversation. if you want the book part clear, use my aunt or my sister rather than she.
i mean my aunt. put both facts together.
when my aunt came home, my sister saw her. my aunt brought a book.
now make it one sentence, keeping the aunt as the person with the book.
my aunt came home with a book, and my sister saw her.
picoboi, make up a simple name for a story about a quiet room and a letter found under a book. do not say it is the name of a real book you found.
one made up name could be: the letter in the quiet room.
now give two more choices using only simple words.
the book by the window. a letter waiting at home.
which one keeps the letter most clear?
the letter in the quiet room keeps the letter and the place clear. the book by the window says more about the book than the letter.
if i choose that first one, do you know my whole story?
no. you gave the quiet room and a letter under a book. the name does not add a whole story unless you ask me to make more.
now i want a short opening with those details.
a person came into the quiet room and moved a book from the table. a letter was under it, with no name on the outside. she sat near the window and looked at the first line.
make the first part simple.
a person came into the quiet room and moved a book from the table. a letter was under it. she sat near the window and looked at the first line.
ask my last request simply.
write the first part of the story with simple words.
